clue.text: It grows abundantly in Tonga, one variety

parts.note: doing something abundantly is doing it well, in plenty
taken as written

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters come out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A plant that flourishes in the Pacific islands of Tonga, one particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges Tonga plus one. 'It grows' is the whole definition: any plant grows, so this is a teasingly vague way to point at a giant tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The wellingtonia is the giant sequoia, a huge conifer, so it is certainly something that grows.

clue.text: Excuse for inadequate lighting in Ireland?

definitions.text: Excuse for inadequate lighting in Ireland?

parts.words: Excuse for inadequate lighting in Ireland?
parts.note: a candle burns dimly when its wick is turned down short; split the Irish county's name into two words and it says just that

explanation.walkthrough: The Irish county name, split into two words, is the reason a candle or oil lamp gives poor light: its wick is low.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is a county on the east coast of Ireland, just south of Dublin, so the place belongs 'in Ireland'.

clue.text: Eg the fabulous bare, in Michelangelo's era

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning the name and era

explanation.surface: A remark placing a fable's hare in the time of the Renaissance artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the answer across Michelange(LO'S ER)A. The hare of Aesop's fable lost the race to the tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's fable the boastful hare is beaten by the tortoise, making it the classic example of the one who fails to win.

clue.text: Club team's man of valour

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a team is a side, and the 's adds the final S

explanation.surface: A golf or sports club's star player praised for his bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Ironsides was the nickname of Oliver Cromwell, and Ironsides were his tough troopers, hence a brave man.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironside is a person of great bravery and hardiness, a name given to heroes such as Cromwell and Edmund Ironside.

clue.text: Not much of a flier, King Cole sounds

indicators.note: sounds signals that we want a word pronounced like the singer's first name

parts.note: Nat King Cole, the American singer and pianist, so the first name is Nat

explanation.surface: Remarking that the crooner Nat King Cole was no great aviator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' says the singer's first name NAT is pronounced the same as the insect's name, whose G is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a tiny fly, so as a flying creature it hardly amounts to much.

clue.text: Changes do imply a period of years

indicators.note: changes as a verb tells us to alter the order of the letters of the words after it

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A statement that alterations suggest a span of several years has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' rearranges DOIMPLYA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an olympiad was the four-year interval between successive Olympic Games.

clue.text: Drive that's lacking at first without a representative

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: that is, abbreviated i.e.
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A motorist's journey that falls short initially, made without a political delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'at first' takes just the opening letter of 'lacking'. 'Drive' looks like a noun about motoring but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge forward, just as driving something forces it onward.

clue.text: Publicity gamble supported by the beak

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece standing on top of another is supported by it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: to play is to gamble, as at the tables
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: An advertising risk that a magistrate has backed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the beak' is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface wants; here it is a bird's bill. 'supported by' puts PLAY above BILL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster advertising a theatre production, so it serves as publicity.

clue.text: Spiritualist meeting Dublin lad, perhaps, before church

indicators.note: before puts the boy's name ahead of the church in the answer

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish boy's name, so an example of a lad from Dublin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A gathering of psychics meets an Irish boy just ahead of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering at which a medium tries to contact the dead, the central ritual of spiritualism.

clue.text: Army scout all over the place as usual

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the two words before are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A soldier on reconnaissance wandering about, as he always does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges ARMYSCOUT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something customary is habitual or normal, just what is usually done.

clue.text: This beats one source of protein!

definitions.meaning: the throb of blood in the arteries, which beats with the heart
peas, beans and lentils, the edible seeds of legumes, rich in protein

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: the heartbeat felt at the wrist, and edible seeds such as lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: The throb felt at the wrist beats with the heart, and lentils, peas and beans are a protein-rich food.

clue.text: Story-teller heard in Bonn is a musician

indicators.note: heard signals that we want only the sound of the word for the teller of tales

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untrue ones
in German, spoken in Bonn, 'is' is ist

explanation.surface: A tale-teller performing in a German city turns out to play music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives LYR, sounding like 'liar'; Bonn was the West German capital, so 'is' there is IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyrist is someone who plays the lyre or writes lyric poetry, a player of an ancient stringed instrument.

clue.text: A woman acting Bunyan's foul Fiend

parts.note: taken as written
Polly is a woman's name
on stage and performing, so on

explanation.surface: A woman performing as the devil in a stage version of a Bunyan story.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bunyan's 'The Pilgrim's Progress' has Christian fight the fiend Apollyon in the Valley of Humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon is the demon whom Christian battles in The Pilgrim's Progress, Bunyan's allegory.

clue.text: Uncanny love for an eccentric

parts.note: something uncanny is strange and eerie, weird
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A strange affection felt for an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is a strange, odd person, which is what an eccentric is, used as a noun.

clue.text: Badges trendy ones gain are fashionable

parts.note: trendy means in fashion, in

indicators.note: read as are fashioned, made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ones written as Roman numerals are I's
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Fashionistas pin on badges because they are in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are fashionable' is read as 'are fashioned', reworking the Roman ones with 'gain'. Roman numeral I standing for one is a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems showing rank, office or membership.

clue.text: Blue a couple of pennies in the county

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the county word

parts.note: a shire is a county
taken as written
P is a penny, so two of them make PP

explanation.surface: Feeling down because of a little money lost in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the enclosing. 'Blue' is a colour here, not a mood, and P for penny is the standard British abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a deep, bright shade of blue named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Cartoon dog and cat about right for Croesus, say

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses the abbreviation for right

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animated dog and a cat circling a rich king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside CAT to give CRAT. Croesus, king of ancient Lydia, was proverbially rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone powerful because of great wealth, and Croesus is the byword for a rich man.

clue.text: Writer takes one sort of wine he regrets

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
one is I, the Roman numeral
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used for communion

explanation.surface: An author has a glass of a particular wine and then is sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT, from Spanish tinto, is a dark red wine from Spain, rare outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitent is a person who repents of wrongdoing, so he is sorry for what he did.

clue.text: One standing up to an army nurse?

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE, a corps of the British Army
a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital

explanation.surface: A question about someone defying a military nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, and in Britain a sister is a senior nurse on a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A resister opposes and defies something, that is, confronts it rather than giving way.

clue.text: Church people concealing a priest's remains

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the priest goes within the church members

parts.note: RCs are Roman Catholics, members of a church
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Churchgoers hiding a cleric's bodily remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' does the enclosing. Eli is the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel, a staple of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are surviving remnants, especially a saint's bones or belongings kept as objects of veneration.

clue.text: Fish from a Scottish island, it's said

indicators.note: said signals that the island's name and the little word are spoken together

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides, followed by the word it from it's

explanation.surface: A catch landed from a Hebridean island, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is an island off the west coast of Scotland; 'Mull it' spoken quickly gives the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullet are a family of food fish, red and grey mullet being common.

clue.text: Sounds like an Asian river-beast

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is pronounced as the river's name

parts.note: the Tigris flows through Turkey and Iraq

explanation.surface: Describing a creature that lives by a river in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' makes the Tigris, the river of Mesopotamia, sound like a female big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, a wild animal.

clue.text: Register arrival of transport at Lincoln's birthplace

parts.note: a log is a record or register, as a ship's log
a taxi that has come is a cab in

explanation.surface: Recording when the coach reached the town where the president was born.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham Lincoln was born in a one-room cabin of logs in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was famously born in a rough timber hut in Kentucky.

clue.text: Scene of conflict causing upset for a long time

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the words over, so they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A battlefield whose trouble has gone on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AN ERA over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest, originally the sanded floor where gladiators fought.

clue.text: Looks like submitting to a technique of Kreisler

definitions.meaning: yielding, bending the head or body in deference
Fritz Kreisler was a famous violinist, and the way a player draws the bow over the strings is a technique

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses with different pronunciations: bending in submission, and a violinist's handling of the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to someone can mean bending low before them, and a violinist's control of the bow is a key skill.

clue.text: Shot decapitated the champ

indicators.note: having lost its head, so the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A gunman shot the boxing title-holder dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the first letter from WINNER. In archery or shooting a shot landing in the ring next to the bull is scored as an inner.
explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting an inner is a hit in the ring just outside the bull, so a type of shot.

clue.text: Border flower coming up in scarlet circle

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a circle looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bloom along a garden edge sprouting within a red ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns RED and O, read upwards, into the answer. A 'flower' is a river (something that flows), here the river on the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder forms much of the border between Germany and Poland, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Ravine where mother abandoned car, perhaps

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the mother's letters leave the word

parts.note: a car is an example of a machine
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A gully where a mum left her vehicle behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes MA from MACHINE. A chine is a southern English word for a deep, narrow ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern England, especially the Isle of Wight and Dorset, a chine is a deep narrow gorge cut through cliffs.

clue.text: Staying power of creed a nun promulgated

indicators.note: promulgated means proclaimed and spread about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A nun's beliefs, spread widely, show her stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promulgated' rearranges CREEDANUN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to keep going through hardship, which is stamina.

clue.text: Chief returned thanks to members — Claggart for one

parts.note: a master is a head or chief

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A boss sending back gratitude to colleagues, with a naval villain as example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TA, British slang for thanks, into AT. John Claggart is the ship's police officer in Melville's 'Billy Budd'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Melville's Billy Budd, Claggart holds the naval rank responsible for discipline on board ship.
